examples_0604

Let matrices \(A\) and \(B\) be defined below.

\[A = \begin{bmatrix} 9 & 8 & 1\\ 4 & 3 & 2\\ 7 & 6 & 5 \end{bmatrix}\] \[B = \begin{bmatrix} 8 & 4 & 7\\ 2 & 9 & 6\\ 3 & 5 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\]

Also, let \(C=AB\) and \(D=BA\).

  • Find element \(d_{2,1}\)

I'd recommend setting up a diagram on (gasp) paper.

When calculating matrix \(D\) with the matrix multiplication \(D=B\cdot A\), the fact that matrix \(B\) is before matrix \(A\) matters (because matrix multiplication is NOT commutative). So, in our diagram, matrix \(B\) is in bottom-left position and matrix \(A\) is in top-right position.


Notice we use row 2 from \(B\) and column 1 from \(A\).

\[d_{2,1}~~=~~2\cdot 9~+~9\cdot 4~+~6\cdot 7\] \[d_{2,1}~~=~~96\]

Let matrices \(A\) and \(B\) be defined below.

\[A = \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 1 & 7\\ 9 & 6 & 8\\ 2 & 3 & 5 \end{bmatrix}\] \[B = \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 6 & 2\\ 8 & 7 & 9\\ 5 & 3 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\]

Also, let \(C=AB\) and \(D=BA\).

  • Find element \(c_{2,1}\)

I'd recommend setting up a diagram on (gasp) paper.

When calculating matrix \(C\) with the matrix multiplication \(C=A\cdot B\), the fact that matrix \(A\) is before matrix \(B\) matters (because matrix multiplication is NOT commutative). So, in our diagram, matrix \(A\) is in bottom-left position and matrix \(B\) is in top-right position.


Notice we use row 2 from \(A\) and column 1 from \(B\).

\[c_{2,1}~~=~~9\cdot 4~+~6\cdot 8~+~8\cdot 5\] \[c_{2,1}~~=~~124\]

Notice we use row 1 from \(A\) and column 2 from \(B\).
